mechanism_narrative: An increase in the Consumer Price Index (CPI) above 2% YoY signals inflationary pressure, leading to tighter monetary policy expectations and negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces positive 20-day returns in > 60% of triggered instances despite negative signal, or CPI YoY > 2% does not lead to tighter monetary policy within the next 3 months.

mechanism_narrative: A decrease in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) below 4% signals a tightening labor market, which leads to wage inflation and increased production costs, resulting in negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces positive 60-day returns in > 60% of triggered instances despite negative signal, or UNRATE < 4% does not lead to wage inflation within the next 6 months.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in Real Final Sales (RSAFS) over three consecutive months signals strengthening consumer demand, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces negative 20-day returns in > 40% of triggered instances despite positive signal, or RSAFS increase does not correlate with improved corporate earnings within the next quarter.

mechanism_narrative: A decrease in Industrial Production (INDPRO) by more than 2% YoY signals a contraction in supply, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces positive 60-day returns in > 60% of triggered instances despite negative signal, or INDPRO YoY < -2% does not lead to a decrease in corporate earnings within the next 6 months.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained 3-month decline in the federal funds rate signals an easing monetary cycle that compresses discount rates applied to equity cash flows, producing positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: Walk-forward Rank IC remains below 0.03 over any 2-year rolling window, or 20-day forward returns in easing periods are not significantly higher than baseline (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: When the unemployment rate (UNRATE) rises above 7% and payroll employment (PAYEMS) decreases for two consecutive months, it signals a weakening labor market, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: UNRATE > 7% and PAYEMS decreases for 2 consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces positive 20-day returns in > 60% of triggered instances despite negative signal, or the combined conditions do not lead to a decrease in consumer spending within the next quarter.

mechanism_narrative: When housing starts (HOUST) increase by more than 10% YoY and real final sales (RSAFS) also increase for two consecutive months, it signals robust demand, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: HOUST YoY > 10% and RSAFS increases for 2 consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces negative 60-day returns in > 40% of triggered instances despite positive signal, or the combined conditions do not lead to improved corporate earnings within the next 6 months.

mechanism_narrative: During a late-cycle expansion, a decrease in Industrial Production (INDPRO) by more than 1% YoY signals a potential supply crunch, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces positive 5-day returns in > 60% of triggered instances despite negative signal, or INDPRO YoY < -1% does not lead to a decrease in corporate earnings within the next month.
